title: Residency lifecycle guard and lightweight KMS proxy for region pin enforcement
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Motivation: Customers operating under regional data residency constraints require cryptographically enforceable, observable controls that prevent use of tenant keys outside allowed regions while preserving a predictable rollout path. This PR introduces a residency lifecycle guard and a lightweight KMS proxy to enforce tenant-region pinning at request time, plus audit metadata enrichment so downstream auditors can verify decisions. The goal is a low-risk, staged deployment path that 1) enforces denial-by-default for disallowed KMS operations, 2) emits continuity evidence to audit logs, and 3) provides a configurable tenant fallback policy (fail/route-to-allowed-region/queue-for-review).

What this PR changes (high level): Adds a residency-guard service that evaluates tenant residency attributes and RBAC v2 policies to make per-request allow/deny/reroute decisions; implements kmsp-proxy-lite (a small proxy sitting in front of the KMS client used by the service runtime) that blocks or rewrites KMS calls when keys are out-of-region; introduces an audit-enricher middleware that attaches residency_evidence headers and a signed decision token to every request forwarded to audit ingestion; extends RBAC v2 templates with a new attribute: tenant.residency.region_pin and a policy snippet in rbac/templates/residency.yaml; provides Helm values and an operator flag to enable the guard in Dedicated and Private installs; and ships tests and docs.

Key design notes: residency-guard is intentionally separated from existing authz flow to avoid coupling; it subscribes to tenant catalog changes and caches pin rules with TTL and versioned checkpoints for fast path checks. kmsp-proxy-lite is single-threaded by design and deliberately minimal: it validates key metadata and origin region, short-circuits unauthorized calls with HTTP 403-style errors to the runtime, and emits a structured audit event on each enforcement action. The audit-enricher attaches a base64-encoded decision envelope signed with the platform audit key (rotatable via KMS). Decision envelopes contain: tenant_id, key_id, requested_operation, resolved_region, rule_version and enforcement_timestamp.

Behavior and rollout plan: feature gated behind operator flag and a feature-flag for Hosted customers. Default rollout uses "monitoring-only" mode where decisions are logged but not enforced; after 2 weeks of telemetry validation the guard flips to "enforce" for a subset of tenants (canary group), then broadens to all tenants. Fallback policy options: fail-request, route-to-allowed-region (if cross-region replication configured), or queue-for-manual-review.

Compatibility: No breaking behavior when disabled. If enabled without corresponding RBAC templates the guard defaults to monitoring-only. KMS providers are supported via a pluggable adapter; we ship adapters for AWS and GCP used in our environments.

Testing: unit tests for the policy matcher and envelope signer; integration tests that run kmsp-proxy-lite against a local KMS emulator; e2e tests in the perf-canary lab that validate latency impact under 99th-percentile load. CI noted a flaky e2e on first run (timing in emulator); test was rerun and passed.

Observability: added residency.guard.* Prometheus metrics (decisions_total, blocked_calls_total, envelope_sign_failures_total), an Alert rule to fire when blocked_calls spike for canary tenants, and new tracing spans (residency.guard.evaluate, kms.proxy.enforce). Audit entries include the signed decision envelope for downstream auditors.

Security review: security team reviewed threat model for envelope signing and key management. The envelope signer uses a short-lived signing key protected by KMS with strict access controls. No plaintext tenant secrets are logged.

Release notes: "Add residency lifecycle guard and lightweight KMS proxy to enforce tenant region pinning. Initial rollout is monitoring-only; operator flag required to enable enforcement. See docs/security/residency-lifecycle.md for configuration and migration steps."

Related work: complements ENG-8110 (residency operator UI) and SEC-1041 (residency audit schema).

Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit/integration tests, [x] docs updated, [x] security review signed, [x] telemetry and alerts added, [x] rollout plan included.

review_comments: Asha Patel: Please add a unit test that covers TTL cache expiry to avoid stale decisions in long-lived processes.
Marisol Vega: Added unit test and a cache invalidation hook; pushed update (see commit a8b3c55).
Liam O'Connor: We should avoid blocking the main request path on a signing call — what if signing KMS is slow? Consider async envelope signing with best-effort attach.
Marisol Vega: Switched to sync-for-monitoring-only and best-effort async path for enforce mode; documented tradeoffs in design notes.

ci_summary: E2E: fail (first run, emulator timing) -> rerun -> pass
Security scan: pass (no high severity findings)
notes: This implementation prioritizes minimal performance impact in the fast path. The kmsp-proxy-lite adds ~1.8ms median overhead in internal perf runs; measured increase at p99 is <6ms in canary environment. Operators should monitor residency.guard.latency and blocked_calls_total when enabling enforcement.
release_notes: Add residency lifecycle guard and lightweight KMS proxy for enforcing tenant region pinning. Operator flag required to enable enforcement. Feature initially ships in monitoring-only mode; see docs for migration steps.
migration_instructions: 1) Enable feature flag in staging and set mode=monitoring. 2) Run for at least 2 weeks and validate signed decision envelopes in audit logs. 3) Enable canary enforcement for a small tenant cohort. 4) Monitor alerts and metrics; escalate via SEC-1041 process if anomalies seen.

audit_impact: Adds structured decision envelopes to audit stream; increases audit event cardinality but improves forensic fidelity. Backfilled envelopes are not provided automatically.
